speakers: George Patterson (Managing Director and CIO, PGIM Quantitative Solutions; transcript spells 'Pim')
summary:
Allocator interview (Ep.35, mid-2026) with the CIO of PGIM Quantitative Solutions (quant equity and multi-asset, $110bn) on systematic macro and multi-asset solutions.
Approach: mid-horizon fundamental regime models (Gaussian mixture, traditional quadrants) plus short-term tactical overlay, many models combined, LLM text analysis, human in the loop.
Conclusions: guard against in-sample optimization, expect faster policy responses, inflation above about 4% is the threshold that hurts, commodities as inflation hedge.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: are the assumptions behind the model still valid? Has there been some regime shift in the data?
claims.claim: Model users must continuously check whether a model's assumptions still hold and whether the data regime has shifted.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: quantitative is a very useful tool but you also have to pay attention to what's going on in the market
claims.claim: Pure model output should be combined with market awareness and a multi-disciplinary team (economics, finance, computer science, math).

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: We still see like an overall positive macro environment for risk assets.
claims.claim: As of mid-2026 PGIM's models see an overall positive macro environment for risk assets, with the US economy surprisingly resilient.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the big opportunities that the the macro concentrated traders have had in the '9s really just don't exist today
claims.claim: Better data and technology mean the large concentrated discretionary macro bets of the 1990s no longer exist; macro investing has become more systematic and nimble.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: web scraping prices we have um you know you can track behavior there's geospatial
claims.claim: Web-scraped prices, behavior tracking and geospatial data now give a much tighter real-time view of consumers than monthly GDP.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: Now, with language processing, you can be monitoring news feeds.
claims.claim: The macro drivers (inflation, growth) are the same, but NLP on news feeds and foreign-language sources gives faster proxies than monthly or quarterly government data.
claims.indicator: NLP news and text measures of inflation and growth

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: where again, you had like uh sudden moves in the bond market that really cause bonds to not work as a defensive instrument
claims.claim: 60/40 fails when bonds stop being defensive (1994, 2022) after sudden bond moves, although 60/40 remains a long-term core.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: you can become much more involved in overlays um or solutions that are going to give you a little bit of convexity or downside protection
claims.claim: Institutions can now obtain diversification through overlays, convexity or downside protection and return stacking; retail has access to derivative income and protection products.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: you largely can't trade them unless you're willing to accept a material discount
claims.claim: Privates cannot be traded without large discounts, so clients seek liquid, systematic ways to return to their strategic allocation.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: there's been one principal component right it's been you know oil's up equity down
claims.claim: Since the Middle East military actions, markets have been dominated by one factor: oil up, inflation up, equities down (or the reverse), so one asset explains the rest.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: advanced language models to kind of see how people are talking about this in the marketplace
claims.claim: PGIM uses language models to track how inflation is discussed plus flow monitoring, to treat inflation as a risk factor.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: if inflation's under 4% you can still do okay with equities
claims.claim: Rule of thumb: below about 4% inflation equities still do fine (commodities gain importance); above 4% there is material impact on fiscal policy and markets.
claims.testable: yes - equity returns by inflation bucket

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the mid- horizon view is much more tied to fundamentals
claims.claim: Mid-horizon regime views come from fundamentals (forward rates, GDP, profits, jobs) and are combined with a short-term tactical view.
claims.indicator: forward rates, GDP, corporate profits, employment

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: have caused us to kind of shrink some of our active exposures just because of the of the really the tactical overlay on top of that
claims.claim: A tactical inflation-risk overlay shrank active exposures while staying pro-risk.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: commodities are still one of the best liquid tools
claims.claim: Commodities are the best liquid inflation hedge, performing especially in inflation shocks, though they are the 'forgotten stepchild' of multi-asset; equities hedge only up to a threshold.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: Gaussian mixture model that basically views the world, views the economy as some sort of unobservable state
claims.claim: A Gaussian mixture model treats the economy as a latent state and classifies regimes from many data points.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: we don't use any like market-based data there because markets can move much faster than the overall economy
claims.claim: The regime model avoids market prices because they move faster than the economy and would contaminate the medium-term economic state.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: where are we in inflation is inflation you know inflation high and rising you know high and falling
claims.claim: Alongside statistical regime models they use a traditional growth/inflation framework (high and rising, high and falling).

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: Often times what you really want to do is you want to combine multiple models together.
claims.claim: No single model is best; combine multiple regime and valuation models rather than trusting one scenario.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: they're all multimodel the winners are usually like a multimodel approach
claims.claim: Winners of Kaggle model competitions use multi-model ensembles, supporting the multi-model approach.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: I think people do get a little too attached to like okay my you know my particular analysis says that you know we're in a regime we're in a regime just like a particular year in the past
claims.claim: Analog thinking ('this is like year X') is a human pattern-matching bias; the thinking goes into model construction, then the model is used if assumptions hold.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the hardest part of this job is being patient and sticking with your guns
claims.claim: The hardest part of systematic investing is sticking to the process during losses and external pressure.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: most of the model probably 80% is really derived on fundamentals
claims.claim: About 80% of the macro model is fundamentals-based, with a small price/statistical component.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: that's when you're going to get nervous and you're going to unplug it because you don't understand it
claims.claim: Purely statistical black-box models get abandoned in underperformance because they cannot be understood; models grounded in economic insight can be held.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the degrees of freedom is very very very few
claims.claim: Macro has few independent observations, so models must be built with explicit priors and insight rather than regression coefficients dropped in.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: We do have some small statistical components um just because again you need to pay attention to those
claims.claim: A small, shorter-term statistical component complements the fundamental macro model.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: you had to kind of get inter you had to intervene in the model because the updates the inputs were just not updated
claims.claim: In COVID, data were released late and inputs (e.g. for cruise lines, airlines) did not update, requiring manual intervention; the investment philosophy comes before the model.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: just going out and buying puts is expensive
claims.claim: Outright puts are expensive; downside protection is better paid for by replacing equity with long-dated call exposure and rebalancing.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: more defensive equity strategies or you know sector rotation that kind of gives you a bit more downside protection
claims.claim: Defensive equity strategies and sector rotation are other cheaper dynamic downside protection routes.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: 2022 when the equity market went down but volatility was moderately high without ever spiking very high and longv kind of strategies didn't provide an enormous amount of convexity
claims.claim: Long-volatility protection paid in COVID but not in 2022 because vol rose moderately without spiking while equities fell.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: That's just been a very rich source of data and a rich source of alpha that we found.
claims.claim: Language models are a rich source of data and alpha for both quant equity and multi-asset.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: in the early days it was like counting positive words versus negative words, which is called the bag of words method
claims.claim: Text-signal methods evolved from bag-of-words counts to BERT/FinBERT sentiment to LLM theme detection, while keeping traceability to raw data.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the ability to extract things both on the alpha side, but more importantly on the risk side have become have just really advanced by leaps and bounds
claims.claim: Text (reports, websites, 10-Ks) is a rich data source, and extraction advances matter more for risk than for alpha.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: Actually, Bird is surprisingly good or Finnbert's surprisingly good in terms of extracting sentiment.
claims.claim: BERT/FinBERT are surprisingly good at sentiment, and LLMs are effective at assessing tone of speeches and text versus past patterns.
claims.indicator: FinBERT sentiment of central bank speech

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: all of these models are only as good as the data they've been trained on
claims.claim: LLMs are statistical next-token predictors only as good as their training data, so evaluation tasks must fit that.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: there are, you know, automated strategies that are that are probably um, you know, in need of uh in in need of, you know, continual refinement and maybe driving prices in the short term
claims.claim: Automated bots may over-react to headlines and drive short-term moves, but evidence is hard to find.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: It's not it's not kind of unconstrained robo trading.
claims.claim: PGIM keeps a human in the loop, with portfolio managers reviewing trades for consistency with the investment philosophy.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: yes certain types of jobs may get eliminated or reduced but other jobs are created
claims.claim: AI follows past technology waves: it eliminates some jobs but creates others and boosts productivity.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: rarely is it accurate. I mean it often times they're forecasting hikes which then never materialize
claims.claim: Rate forward curves rarely predict policy accurately, often pricing hikes or cuts that never occur, so forecasts must be revised and managers nimble.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: as we went into March, we had the strike in Iran and and we had a big reversal in rates
claims.claim: In early 2026 the Citrini report pushed yields down in February, then the March strike in Iran reversed rates, moving the market from pricing cuts to possible hikes.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: at some point they are going to become painful enough. We are going to you know hit the so-called tipping point.
claims.claim: Unresolved US debt to GDP will hit a tipping point, but its timing has no formula, so a nimble stance is needed.
claims.indicator: US debt to GDP, term premium

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: we want to be right a little bit more than 50% of the time
claims.claim: Quant models have only a small edge (right slightly more than 50%); many small bets add up and give a smoother ride than big calls (Moneyball).

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: we want just enough complexity to to do like the to basically do what we need to do
claims.claim: Prefer just enough model complexity to represent the world, leaning simple.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the absolute worst thing you can do is is optimize in sample performance
claims.claim: Optimizing in-sample performance is the worst error; ask what the sample captured and whether it will persist.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: what do you have to do to kill this research?
claims.claim: Researchers must state what assumptions would make their research fail, with a devil's-advocate debate, to guard against overfitting.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: you can always find some period to prove some thesis that you want, but it may not work all the time
claims.claim: With noisy data you can always find a period supporting any thesis, so economic findings must hold across periods.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: if you freeze it at that point once we've gone live what has been the outof sample performance
claims.claim: Freeze parameters at research time and compare live out-of-sample performance; signals are typically positive but weaker than expected.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: usually it's like positive but not as positive as we thought it was
claims.claim: Live signal performance is usually still positive but below the in-sample estimate.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: if that's the case today's parameter should probably be somewhat shorter
claims.claim: If a signal decayed over about 3 months in sample, use somewhat shorter parameters going forward because the world is getting faster.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: policy response is much faster now
claims.claim: Policy responses and crashes are now faster (GFC slow, SVB overnight bank run, COVID record-short move), so shutoffs must be designed in up front.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: If you if you got if you panicked at the bottom of COVID you really missed out on the rebound.
claims.claim: Panic selling at the COVID bottom missed the rebound, so fast V-shaped moves reward staying with the process.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: you can be right in the long run but you just can't afford to maintain the position in the short run
claims.claim: Retail-driven meme stocks can move against a correct model in the short run, so position sizing must survive them.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: that's a that's a feature that's not a problem
claims.claim: Irrational retail investors in equities are a feature that creates opportunity.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: in the equity market, you have retail investors and that's really creates a lot of opportunities
claims.claim: Bonds are mostly institutional with fewer speculative extremes, whereas equities have retail flows that create opportunities, if one avoids the steamroller.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: the tech bubble was all about names that were not profitable
claims.claim: Unlike 1999, today's mega-cap leaders have cash flows, though there are pockets of excess and the AI capex cycle's payoff is unproven.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: I think people have probably ignored emerging markets for a period of time.
claims.claim: Emerging markets have been ignored and changes in earnings plus long-term growth make institutions ask about them as a strategic opportunity.

claims.speaker: George Patterson
claims.quote: it's going to take time for it to become commercially viable
claims.claim: New technologies such as quantum computing take long to move from lab to robust commercial scale, as with semiconductors.
